phrases: What happens to your body in space?
Without gravity squashing your spine, astronauts can grow up to three percent taller.
Back on Earth, they shrink again.
Fluids float up to your head,
so your face gets puffy, and your legs get skinny.
Without exercise, you can lose up to one percent of your bone density every month.
That's why astronauts work out about two hours a day.
And when you close your eyes to sleep,
you might see flashes of light:
cosmic rays zipping through your eyes.
